method.title: How I work
method.intro: Today the programming language matters less than the ability to lead people and agents to a result I answer for.

steps.title: I frame the problem
steps.text: Goals, constraints, architecture and acceptance criteria. This is the part that decides whether a project succeeds, and it stays with me.

steps.title: Agents produce the code
steps.text: Analysis, development, testing and peer review are carried out by AI agents that I direct and verify step by step. I use the same agents to build internal tooling, such as agents that resolve issues on their own.

steps.title: I own the quality
steps.text: Tests, review criteria and shared metrics. I own releases and scope and remain accountable for technical decisions.

method.outcome: With this method my productivity has roughly tripled and quality has improved. I introduced it in the team I lead and I help bring it to the rest of the company, from the way teams work to internal tooling.
method.interest: What interests me is the point where technology and organization meet: how roles, processes and responsibilities change once AI agents are part of everyday work.

blocks.label: Team, people and delivery
blocks.text: I lead a team of 4 to 8 developers depending on active projects and ship an average of 4 projects a year to production, in sectors such as logistics, transportation, public healthcare, energy and fashion. I handle hiring, onboarding and 1:1s, work in Scrum and manage stakeholders, from client to PM. I led a logistics platform on serverless cloud to production, end to end.

blocks.label: AI-native method
blocks.text: I introduced an AI-agent-based way of working in the team, from analysis to peer review, and defined its review criteria and metrics. When production issues arise, I work back from the data to the root cause.

blocks.label: AI transition and pre-sales
blocks.text: I have built internal tools such as autonomous agents for issue resolution and a shared library of plugins and skills, and I am defining a framework to assess AI usage across company roles. For clients I deliver generative AI solutions (computer vision, document extraction and classification, RAG, multi-agent systems) and prepare about 10 estimates a year for new prospects.

projects.title: Outside of work
projects.intro: In my spare time I apply the same method to my own projects: I decide what to build and how, AI agents write the code, and I own the result.

items.name: A homelab run with AI agents
items.text: Two servers: a home server for virtualization and home automation, and a cloud server with self-hosted services. I administer them with Claude Code, treating the infrastructure the way I would treat a team.
highlights: Operational documentation written for the agents: current state, reasoned constraints and known pitfalls
Every documentation update goes through a reviewer subagent and automated checks
Claude Code connected to Home Assistant via MCP for automations and dashboards
Nightly encrypted backups to a remote server and a clean shutdown on power outages

items.name: Fiabino
